# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 1 (Bu-Vb Np1)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np1
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 1
**Title (English, from literature):** The training rule on keeping extra robe-cloth beyond ten days
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kathina* training rule, categorized as Nissaggiya Pācittiya 1 in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya, stipulates that a monk who keeps extra robe-cloth (*cīvara*) for more than ten days commits an offense that requires both forfeiture of the cloth and confession. Akira Hirakawa observes that this precept—often designated in the traditions by the key phrase "ten days"—is an obligation shared in common by both monks and nuns; because its complete formulation and commentary are set forth in the *Bhikkhu-vinaya*, the rule's analytical text is omitted in the Pali *Bhikkhunī-vinaya* [Hirakawa 1982]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying vibhaṅga has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
